# cutver 0.20.0 — 2026-11-20

This release turns the release itself into a contract. Three new surfaces make the pipeline inspectable
instead of narrated: `cutver plan` says what a release will do without doing it, `cutver attest` records a
gate's verdict so `publish` can refuse a claim nobody verified, and the CI channel writes what the
workflow used to parse out of a log. Alongside them, every JSON surface carries a `schemaVersion`, and the
project's own release workflow reads the tool's step outputs instead of a report file.

It is also a hardening release: 27 pull requests, and 14 of them are documentation, contract and
maintenance work rather than product surface. Both halves are below, because a fork inherits both.

Two changes are visible to a consumer that parses cutver's output. They come first, with what to change.

## Breaking changes

**Every JSON object opens with `schemaVersion: 1`** ([#327](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/327)).
This covers `bump --json`, `bump --report`, `changelog latest --json`, `changelog show --json`,
`plugin list --json`, `plugin info --json` and `plugin search --json`. The rule for version 1 is additive:
keys only get added, so a consumer that ignores unknown keys reads the same values it read before. The one
shape change is `plugin search --json`, which printed a bare array — an array has nowhere to put a version,
so it emits `{"schemaVersion": 1, "plugins": [...]}` and callers read `.plugins[]` instead of `.[]`.

*To migrate*: read `schemaVersion` first and branch on a value you were not written for. Only
`plugin search --json` needs a parser change for version 1: `.plugins[]` instead of `.[]`.

**A failure under machine output is one JSON object on stderr**
([#328](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/328)). When the invocation asked for machine output — `--json`,
plus `--report` for `bump` — a failure is exactly this, on one line:

```json
{"schemaVersion":1,"error":{"code":"config","exitCode":1,"message":"…"}}
```

*To migrate*: stop grepping the human sentence. The class is `.error.code` (a stable string), the exit
status is unchanged, and `.error.message` carries the text you were matching before.

## `cutver plan`: the release as data, and nothing else
[#329](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/329)

`cutver plan [--json]` computes the release the workspace is about to cut and changes nothing: no write, no
stage/commit/tag/push, no preflight, no `[hooks]`, no `[publish] commands` — and no plugin dispatch at all,
not even `on_pre_bump`, which `bump --dry-run` still dispatches. That is what makes it safe on a dirty tree
and on a branch that is not `main`, which is where a CI job needs to plan.

The plan is derived, not described: the same code that runs the bump produces it, so a `plan` that
disagrees with a `bump` has one place to look. Blockers are data — a dirty tree, a mismatched
`require_branch`, an existing release tag — and a blocked plan still exits 0, because a plan you can read
is the point. Exit 1 means it could not compute one.

## `cutver attest`: a gate's verdict as a fact
[#331](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/331) · `[gates]` in `cutver.toml`

```bash
cutver attest ci --commit "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" --conclusion success --run "$RUN_URL"
```

A gate is a name, a commit, a conclusion and the day it was recorded, written as one JSON object under
`[gates] dir` (default `.cutver/attestations`). `publish` then requires every gate named by
`[gates] require` plus every `--require-gate` on the invocation, deduplicated, and refuses a missing
attestation or a recorded failure before the tag exists. "This was verified" stopped being a sentence in a
workflow and became something the tool refuses on.

Declared artifacts carry the other half ([#330](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/330)): the files a
release promises are downloaded and their digests verified before the tag is created, so a release that
cannot produce its assets never gets a tag.

## The CI channel: the tool writes what the workflow used to parse
[#332](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/332) · [#342](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/342)

Detection is `GITHUB_ACTIONS` true plus a writable `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` or `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, and the
channel is on by default when detected. `--ci` and `--no-ci` are global flags, so a runner can always turn
it off — a flag that silently does nothing is the defect this release exists to remove.

- `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` gets the field names the machine payload already carries, one `key=value` per line:
  `released`, `deferred`, `version`, `tag`, `commit` for `bump`; `next_version`, `tag`, `commit` for
  `plan`. A value the run does not have is omitted rather than written empty, which is why a `--dry-run`
  bump writes no `commit` line.
- `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` gets one bounded markdown block per run. Text that originates in your content — a
  changelog entry, a commit subject — is escaped or fenced, so it cannot inject structure.
- On failure, one `::error::` line goes to stderr carrying the same text as the human error. Nothing is
  added to stdout, so the machine contract ("stdout is the payload") stays literally true.

This repository's own `release.yml` now reads those outputs instead of parsing a JSON report with `jq`
([#342](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/342)), and its bump step fails closed when the outputs are
missing or the value is not one of the two the gated jobs compare against.

## Release notes: a stream, and sections for templates
[#310](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/310) · [#311](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/311)

`cutver publish --notes-file -` reads the notes from standard input, and an empty stream fails closed with
`release notes on stdin were empty` before the tag, the pushes or the publish commands run. A streamed run
declares no path in the worktree, so a transient notes file stops being something the clean-tree guard has
to know about.

Custom note templates now receive `sections` in the release context: an ordered sequence of
`{heading, entries, is_breaking}`, resolved once by the host. A breaking entry appears in the breaking
section only, empty sections are omitted, and a release with no commits yields an empty sequence.

## Fixes

- **Hooks are bounded, with a tree kill** ([#314](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/314)): both hook
  kinds share the supervised spawn preflight already used, so a hook that outlives its timeout no longer
  leaves descendants holding the pipes.
- **The tag prefix is read where it is written**
  ([#312](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/312), [#313](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/313)):
  `changelog` reads existing headings through the configured prefix, and `doctor` lists changelog versions
  through it too.
- **The install action verifies what it installs** ([#325](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/325)):
  `cutver/setup` checks the release's `SHA256SUMS` before extracting and fails closed, pinned by commit.

## Maintenance and documentation

The other 14 pull requests, grouped by what a fork inherits:

- **An enforceable contract.** `CONTRACT.md` was re-evaluated against reality rather than intention: the
  binary-size budget that nothing enforced is gone, replaced by a lean dependency-shape invariant that
  `cargo tree` can check; the surviving numbers each name their checker; and the rule "every declaration
  ships with its check" is now itself enforced by new tests for CLI/docs parity, documentation examples,
  documentation links and the dependency shape ([#336](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/336),
  [#340](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/340)). The queue of work that had to precede this phase was
  written down before it started ([#335](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/335)).
- **Templates for the maintenance itself.** Issue forms for a bug, a feature and contract debt, plus a pull
  request template carrying the checklists this project applies by hand, pinned by a test
  ([#337](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/337)).
- **A local gate that mirrors CI.** `scripts/check.sh` runs the workflow's steps in its order, in the
  environment Actions gives them, and reports what this host cannot run instead of passing quietly; a
  ratchet keeps the source-line ceiling from drifting ([#333](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/333)).
- **Documentation rebuilt around the two-phase release**: getting started teaches `init` → `doctor` →
  `plan` → `bump --defer-publish` → notes → `publish --notes-file -` with transcripts captured from a
  scratch repository, the tour and FAQ answer for `plan`, the reference pages were split off their line
  ceiling, and the plugin pages were rewritten concept-first with the reference plugin on its own page
  ([#334](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/334), [#338](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/338),
  [#339](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/339), [#340](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/340),
  [#315](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/315), [#319](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/319)).
- **A 57-second film and its accessibility page**, embedded in the README
  ([#309](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/309)).
- **`cutver/release` deprecated** in favour of the commands, with a migration guide, and the installed
  skills catalog resynced with the corrections
  ([#323](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/323), [#320](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/320)).
- **One flaky test removed at the root**: the invalid-semver plugin fixture now consumes its invocation
  envelope before answering, so a linux run cannot lose the plugin's answer to a broken pipe
  ([#341](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/pull/341)).

## What this release does not include

- Phases 5 and 6 of [#326](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/issues/326): `--channel` with promotion and
  `publish --resume`, and declared per-phase needs with `--root`. The CI contract is complete through
  phase 4; those two are open.
- The attestation section on the two integration pages. `cutver attest` and `--require-gate` are documented
  in the [CLI reference](https://github.com/cutver/cutver/blob/main/docs/reference/cli.md); the end-to-end
  flow on the GitHub Actions pages is still missing and tracked.
- This release was cut by the pipeline it describes, and that dispatch is the only place its own workflow
  was exercised for real: no test executes a workflow. The dry-run dispatch before it proved the branch
  where nothing publishes; this one proved the branch where everything does.
